title.narrative: ERSKID/KIB M1-32FOD-000227 UN-HABITAT´S SUPPORT TO URBAN 2030 - MONITORING AND REPORTING OF THE URBAN AND TERRITORIAL DIMENSIONS OF SDGS Phase 2 (URBAN2030)

description.narrative:
Background As facilitator of the United Nations system-wide strategy for sustainable urban development and United Nations focal point on sustainable urbanization and human settlements, UN-Habitat monitors and reports on global conditions and trends. The agency also leads and coordinates the implementation of the New Urban Agenda in collaboration with other United Nations system agencies. UN-Habitat endeavours to strengthen the use of innovative urban solutions, as well as robust data and analysis generated through the City Prosperity Index, global/national samples of cities, spatial analytics and urban observatories, among others, to support the global monitoring of the Goals, the New Urban Agenda and other global frameworks. UN-Habitat and the European Union have a close cooperation concerning global agendas in the field of urban development. Important milestones were the adoption of the Sustainable Development Goals in 2015 and the New Urban Agenda in 2016 at the Habitat III conference, during which the European Union pledged to contribute a proposal for a unified definition on the degree of urbanization. The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the New Urban Agenda call for collection of harmonized indicators for cities and urban and rural areas to support consistent international comparisons across countries. However, an internationally developed and agreed harmonized method to delineate these areas was not available previously. National definitions vary significantly, adversely affecting international comparisons. Consequently, in its 51st session, in March 2020, the United Nations Statistical Commission endorsed a methodology called “degree of urbanization” for delineation of cities and urban and rural areas for international and regional statistical comparison purposes. The method was proposed by a consortium of international organisations (EU, OECD, World Bank, FAO, UN-Habitat, ILO) led by the EU. The UN General Assembly, in a resolution in December 2020, called “upon UN-Habitat to continue to provide normative guidance and operational support to cities and human settlements […] (b) by supporting efforts of the Statistical Commission to establish a functional definition of urban areas and develop a common methodology for aggregating subnational urban statistics;” The EU-led consortium proposing the methodology for defining a “degree of urbanization” is expected to report back to the UN Statistical Commission on its implementation. While details remain to be confirmed, a report could be submitted in 2024-25. The project will be implemented in the context of the ongoing cooperation of UN-Habitat, the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Regional and Urban Policy, and the Joint Research Centre on reporting the urban and territorial dimensions of implementing the Agenda 2030 in the EU . UN-Habitat has implemented the EU-funded project “UN-Habitat’s support to URBAN 2030 - Monitoring and reporting of the urban and territorial dimensions of SDGs” between 2019 and 2022 which aimed at increasing coherence between EU and global agendas and which made a series of recommendations on furthering SDG indicators related to urban development. UN Habitat is a key partner in the Urban Agenda of the European Union that is the key delivery mechanism of the New Urban Agenda. The UN General Assembly decided to convene a high-level event in April of 2022 to take stock of the New Urban Agenda. The UN Secretary General will present the second quadrennial report on the New Urban Agenda. Both will count on the preparation and contributions of UN-Habitat and its partners, including governments and the EU.
Objective The general objective of the programme is to contribute to the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals and the New Urban Agenda. Furthermore, it will increase the awareness and visibility of the work of DG Regio, the JRC and UN-Habitat on SDG indicators and UN Statistics on Human Settlements. The specific objectives are: • to support the implementation of the methodology Degree of Urbanization for delineation of cities and urban and rural areas for international comparison purposes and the UN General Assembly Resolution A/RES/75/224 which calls upon UN-Habitat to support the implementation of the latter. • to enable the development of the territorial dimension of 2030 Agenda. • to refine the indicators linked to the Sustainable Development Goals by exploring linkages of territorial, population and economic indicators, therefore capturing the transformative power of urbanization.
